attributes.title: Beacons
attributes.lede: Out of the button. Into the bin.
attributes.sample: {{! Compose and Trash live in the chrome, OUTSIDE the region. Neither is a participant — a beacon is never inserted, kept or removed, and moving one never starts a run. It only says where it is. }} {{#each this.rows key='id' as |row|}} {{/each}} {{! a new row borrows Compose's box as a start it never had }} {{! a deleted row borrows Trash's box as an end it never reaches. layoutId could not do this: it pairs two REAL elements and morphs one into the other, so the bin itself would stretch. }} {{! and the tray closes up around the gap }}

lesson.concept: A destination can be a place rather than an item
lesson.why: Compose and Trash are beacons outside the list region. A row borrows their bounds without turning the toolbar controls into participants or stretching the trash can.
lesson.experiment: Delete a row, then change another row before the flight finishes. Compare the departing row with the neighbours closing its gap.
lesson.pitfall: Using layoutId for the bin makes an identity morph where the intent is a flight to a location.
lesson.combine: Combine with far matching when the destination really contains a persistent copy of the same item.
